meta.description: Clinical Research Bias Assessment - Case-Control Study (NOS) v2.3.0. Use when you need to assess the bias of a case-control study using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) criteria, or when evaluating the quality of a medical paper.

scientific_integrity.detail: Uses established NOS criteria for case-control study quality assessment

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for quality assessment of published studies, not clinical decisions

methodological_ground.detail: Based on Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, a validated tool for assessing study quality

code_usability.detail: No bundled scripts; assessment workflow is analysis-based using NOS criteria

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive NOS assessment covering Selection (4 items), Comparability (1 item), Exposure (3 items)

reliability.note: Clear NOS criteria and scoring system; minor: no worked examples of completed assessments

performance_context.note: Well-structured workflow with assessment domains; minor: no reference files for detailed criteria

agent_usability.note: Clear when-to-use guidance, structured output format, NOS domains documented; minor: signaling questions not fully enumerated

human_usability.note: Clear workflow and output format; minor: quick validation mentions scripts/extract_pdf.py that doesn't exist

security.note: Excellent security: local analysis only, no network calls, PHI handling warnings included

maintainability.note: Version 2.3.0 documented, MIT license, clear changelog in POLISH_CHANGELOG.md

agent_specific.note: Good scope definition and failure handling; minor: escape hatch for studies outside NOS scope not explicit, script reference inconsistency

inputs.label: Assess case-control study using NOS criteria

assertions.note: Case definition, representativeness, control selection, control definition
Domain → Item → Comments → Quote → Score pattern
NOS allows for unclear/not reported items

assertions.text: Comments explain what information is missing

assertions.note: Output format doesn't explicitly require limitations section

inputs.label: Assess cohort study using NOS
inputs.note: Correctly identified as wrong study design

assertions.note: Skill name and description specify case-control studies
Different NOS criteria apply to cohort studies
No explicit pointer to cohort NOS skill or criteria
When to Use section clarifies case-control focus

key_strengths: Clear Newcastle-Ottawa Scale implementation with all 8 assessment items (Selection 4, Comparability 1, Exposure 3)
Structured output format with domain → item → comments → quote → score pattern for reproducibility
Good version control with v2.3.0 documented and POLISH_CHANGELOG.md tracking changes
Appropriate practice boundaries with warnings about credentials, privacy, and safety constraints
Strong security with local-only analysis and PHI handling guidance

recommendations.title: Remove or fix script reference inconsistency
recommendations.problem: Quick Validation section mentions scripts/extract_pdf.py but scripts directory doesn't exist
recommendations.root_cause: Documentation copied from template or previous version with bundled scripts
recommendations.fix: Remove Quick Validation section entirely or update to: 'No scripts required. Provide the study text or PDF and follow the NOS assessment workflow.'

recommendations.title: Add explicit escape hatch for cohort studies
recommendations.problem: Case-control focus clear but no redirect for cohort studies
recommendations.root_cause: Scope boundary lacks alternative tool guidance
recommendations.fix: Add to When to Use: 'For cohort studies, use cohort-study-quality-assessment-nos. For other designs (RCTs, cross-sectional), use design-specific quality assessment tools.'

recommendations.title: Add limitations section to output format
recommendations.problem: No explicit guidance to document assessment limitations when information is unclear
recommendations.root_cause: Output format doesn't include summary/limitations section
recommendations.fix: Add to Output Format: 'After all domains, include: **Assessment Limitations**: Document any unclear items, missing information, or assumptions made during assessment.'
